newsitem.title: USA: Nebraska fed cattle trade quiet after jumping $4.
newsitem.headline: Nebraska fed cattle trade quiet after jumping $4.

text.p: Nebraska feedlot cattle trade was quiet, with no bids or sales reported after this week's active sales when prices surged as much as $4.00 per cwt on cattle sold on a dressed basis, market sources said.
"We basically sold everything there was to sell," one source said.
Weekly sales totalled about 83,300 head in Nebraska, USDA said. While some cattle sold at $108.00 on a dressed basis Thursday, most sold at $106.00 to $107.00/dressed Wednesday.
Price gains were tied to firm demand for beef and tight supplies of finished animals, sources said.
